{{Short description|French mathematician}}
{{Hatnote|Not to be confused with the French politician [[Paul Reynaud]].}}

[[File:Reyneau - Analyse demontrée, 1739 - 4604591.tif|thumb|''Analyse demontrée'', 1739]]
'''Charles-René Reynaud''' (or '''Reyneau'''), (1656, [[Brissac-Quincé|Brissac]], Province of Anjou – 24 February 1728, Paris) was a French mathematician.

== Biography ==
A priest of the [[Oratory of Saint Philip Neri]], father Reyneau was successively professor of philosophy at [[Toulon]] and [[Pézenas]], and then of mathematics at the college of [[Angers]]. He was a member of the {{Interlanguage link|Académie des sciences, belles-lettres et arts d'Angers|fr}} and free associate of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].

His ''Analyse démontrée'' is a collection of the main theories prevalent in works of (?) etc.; Reyneau added demonstrations or offered better ones.

== Publications ==
* ''Analyse démontrée, ou la Méthode de résoudre les problèmes de mathématiques'', Paris, 1708, 2 t., in one vol. [[Quarto|in-4°]]
** Several editions online at [[HathiTrust|HathiTrust Digital Library]], including [http://onlinebooks.library.upenn.edu/webbin/book/browse?type=atitle&index=1050701&key=reyneau&c=x la deuxième, Paris, Quillau, 1736-1738]
* ''Science du calcul des grandeurs en général, ou Éléments de mathématiques'', Paris, J. Quillau, 1714–35, 2 vol. in-4°, with figures
** [http://hdl.handle.net/2027/mdp.39015068506594 Edition online at HathiTrust]
